# Copilot code review — wedding-app

Private **SvelteKit (Svelte 5) + TypeScript** wedding website: invited guests log in with an invitation
code to RSVP, request a room booking, and read the day's info. SSR via `@sveltejs/adapter-node`, deployed
as an OCI-packaged Kustomize tenant on the devantler-tech platform cluster. Canonical conventions live in
[`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md); this is the concise review checklist — flag violations of the rules below.

## Always (every PR)

- **Conventional-Commit PR title** (`feat:`/`fix:`/`docs:`/`ci:`/`chore:`/`refactor:`/`test:`). The
  squash-merge title feeds semantic-release, so a non-conventional or bracket-prefixed title is a defect.
- **Root-cause fixes only.** Flag anything that masks a failure instead of fixing it: checks skipped or
  set `continue-on-error` to dodge red CI, deleted/weakened assertions, `--no-verify`, silenced linters.
- **Never hand-edit generated files.** Here: `drizzle/` SQL migrations + metadata (regenerate with
  `npm run db:generate`) and `package-lock.json` (let npm regenerate). Flag manual edits to either.
- **Behaviour / route / API / schema / config / UX change ⇒ its docs updated in the same PR**
  (`README.md` / `AGENTS.md`). A missing doc update is a review finding.
- **No secrets in plaintext** — flag committed `DATABASE_URL`, tokens, `.env`, or kubeconfigs.
  `deploy/*.enc.yaml` are SOPS-encrypted (Flux decrypts in-cluster); a *decrypted* secret in a diff is a defect.
- PRs from the Daily AI Assistant carry a `> 🤖 Generated by the Daily AI Assistant` line — expected, not a finding.

## SvelteKit + TypeScript

- Svelte 5 **runes** (`$state`/`$derived`/`$props`); flag legacy `export let` / reactive `$:` in new code.
  Keep TypeScript strict — no new `any`, no `// @ts-ignore` to dodge a real type error.
- `npm run check` (svelte-kit sync && svelte-check) and `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config,
  `eslint-plugin-svelte` + `typescript-eslint`) must pass — they are required CI checks.
- TailwindCSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`); prefer utility classes over ad-hoc `<style>`.
- Unit tests are **Vitest** (`tests/unit/`), E2E is **Playwright** (`tests/e2e/`). New behaviour ⇒ a test;
  don't delete a failing test to go green.

## Server, auth & data (security-sensitive)

- Server-only code lives in `src/lib/server/` (`auth`, `cookies`, `db`, `schema`, `validate-session`,
  `migrate`, `seed`). It must **never** be imported into client/`+page.svelte` code — that leaks secrets and
  DB access to the browser. Flag any such import.
- Auth is invitation-code login + session cookies via `src/hooks.server.ts`. Scrutinise changes that touch
  session validation, cookie flags (httpOnly/secure/sameSite), or route guards for **auth bypass**.
- `DEV_SKIP_AUTH=true` is for local/E2E only (forms return mocks, no Postgres). Flag any path that lets it
  weaken auth in a production build.
- Drizzle ORM + Postgres (`pg`): use parameterised queries / the query builder — flag raw string-interpolated SQL.

## Validation & CI

- Mirror `ci.yaml`: `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run check && npm test && npm run test:e2e && npm run build`.
- Private platform-tenant app — be conservative; never expose its contents publicly.

When unsure, defer to [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) and its `## Maintenance` section.
